_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.register: neutral, works for teens and adults
phrases.content_surface: title, meta, H1, hero, locales/fr.json sitewide chrome
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head term for the whole fancy-text category. Use as the main H1/title anchor; do not overuse as filler inside every sentence.
phrases.good_example: Texte stylé : générateur d'écriture stylée à copier-coller (Insta, TikTok, Discord)

phrases.content_surface: page title (fr/police-d-ecriture/), platform pages (police-instagram, police-tiktok, police-discord, police-snapchat), FAQ
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the "browse by font family" framing (as opposed to "pseudo"/"écriture" framings which target different intents). Pairs naturally with platform names: "police Instagram", "police Discord".
phrases.good_example: Police Discord — Écriture Discord à Copier-Coller (Sans Nitro)

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as an aesthetic-framing alternative to "écriture stylée" when the pitch is about elegance/prettiness rather than customization/gaming.
phrases.good_example: "La beauté d'une écriture, c'est subjectif — c'est pour ça que cette page affiche tous les styles au lieu d'en imposer un."
phrases.avoid_when: gaming/tryhard contexts - reads too soft there

phrases.usage_guidance: "Aesthetic" is kept as an untranslated English loanword deliberately - this matches how French teens actually talk about this subculture online (no natural French equivalent carries the same meaning). Do not force a French translation like "esthétique" - that reads clinical/wrong register.
phrases.good_example: "L'écriture aesthetic, c'est ce style doux et travaillé qu'on voit partout dans les bios Instagram et les profils TikTok."

phrases.usage_guidance: The pillar term for the whole nickname-generator use case. "Pseudo" (not "nom d'utilisateur") is the natural French word for username in gaming/social contexts.
phrases.good_example: Pseudo stylé — générateur de pseudo ꧁꧂ à copier-coller

phrases.content_surface: FAQ ("C'est quoi un pseudo tryhard ?"), ready-made name section
phrases.usage_guidance: "Tryhard" is a fully borrowed English gaming term, used as-is (no French calque exists that carries the same meaning). Pair with the specific symbol vocabulary (亗, シ, ツ, 彡, 乂) that French players associate with the style.
phrases.good_example: "Un pseudo «tryhard», c'est le style des joueurs sweat : court, agressif, avec des symboles japonais comme 亗 (couronne), シ / ツ (sourire), 彡 (vent) ou 乂."

phrases.content_surface: pervasive: titles, buttons, meta descriptions, step-by-step instructions across nearly every fr/ page
phrases.usage_guidance: The single most load-bearing action phrase on the whole site. Standard, correct French (confirmed by Quebec's own OQLF Vitrine linguistique glossary entry for "copier-coller"), not an anglicism.
phrases.good_example: "Écris ton nom dans la barre en haut de la page... Touche «Copier» à côté du style qui te plaît, puis colle-le."

phrases.usage_guidance: This is how French players literally phrase the search query, confirmed across three independent gaming-forum threads over multiple years. Use as an H2/section label, not just buried in prose.
phrases.good_example: "Caractères spéciaux pour pseudo — les cadres ꧁꧂"

phrases.usage_guidance: Broader/more formal umbrella term than "symboles" - use in titles/schema alternateName fields where search intent may use either word.
phrases.good_example: alternateName: ["Pseudo Stylé", ..., "Caractères Spéciaux Pseudo"]

phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the specific "put a space in a name field that rejects spaces" job. Distinct from the broader "caractère invisible" (which also covers fully-blank names).
phrases.good_example: "Pseudo avec espace (caractère invisible)"

phrases.usage_guidance: Long-standing, extremely stable community term - use as the canonical head term for the whole invisible-text feature.
phrases.good_example: Texte Invisible (Caractère Invisible) — Copier-Coller un Espace Vide

phrases.content_surface: JSON-LD alternateName, FAQ ("Comment faire un pseudo invisible sur Free Fire ou Mobile Legends ?")
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the specific job of making a name field appear totally blank, as opposed to "espace invisible" (a space mid-name).
phrases.good_example: alternateName: ["Texte Invisible", "Caractère Invisible", "Espace Vide", "Pseudo Vide", ...]

phrases.content_surface: FAQ across multiple pages, live name-checker warning text in js/gamename/game-rules.js
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the site's standard, recurring way of describing tofu/fallback-glyph failure - reuse verbatim rather than re-describing the phenomenon differently per page. Already wired into the live Free Fire name-checker's warning copy ("Peut s'afficher en carrés ▯ sur certains téléphones").
phrases.good_example: "Certaines polices ou certains symboles rares ne sont pas supportés par tous les serveurs de jeu et s'affichent en carrés (▯)."

phrases.content_surface: FAQ ("Pourquoi mon pseudo Free Fire est-il refusé")
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for official/error-message-flavored contexts (mirrors actual platform error copy). "Pseudo refusé" is the more casual player-facing equivalent for the same failure.
phrases.good_example: "Pourquoi mon pseudo Free Fire est-il refusé ou s'affiche en carrés ?"

phrases.content_surface: FAQ, live name-checker copy, ecriture-bio platform selector
phrases.usage_guidance: Always pair the abstract term with the concrete per-platform number - the site does this consistently and it reads as more trustworthy/specific than a vague "there's a limit" statement.
phrases.good_example: "Le champ pseudo de Free Fire accepte 12 caractères, et les symboles Unicode décoratifs comptent double."

phrases.content_surface: editorial body copy on fr/petite-ecriture (the page itself titles as "petite écriture", using "petites majuscules" as the technical in-body label for the small-caps sub-style)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use "petites majuscules" as the precise technical label for the small-caps sub-style within the broader "petite écriture" (small text) page; "small caps" itself is also used untranslated as a secondary label.
phrases.good_example: "Small caps — des majuscules miniatures : ʙᴏɴᴊᴏᴜʀ. Le look propre et différent, parfait pour un nom ou une bio."

phrases.usage_guidance: Standard, safe term with a live dedicated page - use freely as the anchor for the blackletter style family.
phrases.good_example: n/a (page title only confirmed via grep)

phrases.content_surface: not confirmed as a dedicated fr/ page in this audit
phrases.usage_guidance: Likely accessible only via the main generator's style filter tabs, not a titled standalone page - verify before citing as an SEO-targeted phrase.
phrases.good_example: n/a
phrases.avoid_when: do not claim this has a dedicated ranking page without checking styles.js CATEGORY_PAGES first

phrases.content_surface: page titles across the kaomoji library cluster
phrases.usage_guidance: "Kaomoji" (not translated) is the standard term across the whole cluster (kaomoji, cute-kaomoji, love-kaomoji, cat-kaomoji). "Smiley japonais" is used as a secondary/explanatory gloss, not the primary label.
phrases.good_example: Kaomoji (◕‿◕) : Copier-coller de visages textuels japonais (mignon, chat, amour)

phrases.native_phrase: nom de guilde / tag de guilde
phrases.usage_guidance: "Guilde" is the Free Fire-specific in-game menu term (confirmed by the page's own FAQ describing the exact menu path: Free Fire → menu Guilde → paramètres). "Tag" and "squad" are used as supporting borrowed-English terms for the shorter marking ("tag de guilde", "nom de squad").
phrases.good_example: "Ouvre Free Fire → menu Guilde → icône des paramètres de la guilde."
phrases.avoid_when: do not substitute "clan" for "guilde" on Free Fire pages specifically - it doesn't match the game's own UI label

phrases.content_surface: not yet used in repo; relevant to fr/imprimables/ printables cluster
phrases.usage_guidance: This is a genuine FR/QC terminology divergence worth flagging for the printables cluster specifically: France's Éducation nationale and general French usage default to "cursive" (confirmed live on fr/imprimables/alphabet-cursif/), while Québec pedagogical sources (LEARN Québec, Psychomédia) more commonly frame the same distinction as "lettres attachées" vs. "lettres détachées/moulées". If/when the printables cluster gets QC-specific attention, consider this pairing rather than assuming "cursive" alone covers it.
phrases.good_example: "Lettres détachées ou lettres attachées?" (LEARN Québec blog title)
phrases.avoid_when: do not use "lettres attachées" as if it were the FR-market-standard term - France's own printables page already correctly uses "cursif/cursive"

phrases.usage_guidance: Do NOT use "kikoo"-style abbreviated/SMS-speak phrasing in on-site copy, and do not use the word itself as a keyword or brand voice element - French Wikipedia confirms it is explicitly pejorative, signaling immaturity/poor communication. Useful only as a negative signal: it marks what register to avoid.
phrases.good_example: n/a (this is an avoid-list entry, not a usage example)
phrases.avoid_when: always - this is dated 2000s-2010s slang with a mocking connotation, not a usable brand-voice term

phrases.usage_guidance: "Glitch" is kept untranslated (standard borrowed tech/gaming term in French); "maudit" (cursed) and "effrayant" (scary/creepy) are the natural French adjectives used alongside it. Matches the Discord guide's own framing of zalgo as visually disruptive.
phrases.good_example: "Le résultat semble glitché, maudit ou corrompu, avec des diacritiques empilés de façon chaotique."

phrases.native_phrase: compteur de mots et de caractères
phrases.content_surface: dedicated page title/H1; per-platform limit selector on ecriture-bio
phrases.usage_guidance: Pairs naturally with concrete numbers per platform (already the pattern on fr/usecase/ecriture-bio/: "150 caractères pour la bio" Instagram, "190 caractères" Discord, etc.) - always give the number, not just the tool name.
phrases.good_example: "Choisis ta plateforme (Instagram, TikTok, Discord, X ou Tinder) pour que le compteur corresponde à sa limite de bio."

phrases.native_phrase: changeur de police / convertisseur de casse
phrases.usage_guidance: Straightforward utility naming, safe to use as-is. "Casse" (case, as in upper/lowercase) is standard French typographic vocabulary, not an anglicism.
phrases.good_example: Majuscules et Minuscules — Convertisseur de Casse en Ligne

phrases.usage_guidance: "Sweaty" (English) is used untranslated in the SEO title ("Pseudo Sweaty") while body copy uses the semi-Frenchified "joueurs sweat" - both forms are live on-site simultaneously; this is consistent with how the term is actually used in French gaming communities (borrowed wholesale, only lightly adapted).
phrases.good_example: Symboles Fortnite ツ 亗 乂 — à Copier-Coller pour Pseudo Sweaty (2026)

phrases.usage_guidance: "Coquette" here refers to the specific 2020s internet aesthetic subculture (bows, ribbons, soft-feminine), not the older standard French adjective meaning "flirtatious" - context distinguishes them, but be aware of the double meaning when writing surrounding copy.
phrases.good_example: Symboles Coquette 🎀 Nœuds, Rubans & Cœurs Aesthetic à Copier-Coller

phrases.usage_guidance: Correctly distinguishes "usurpation" (impersonation risk) from generic "pseudo stylé peut-il faire bannir" fear - this precision matches Discord's actual moderation model and is more accurate than the vaguer ban-fear framing used on other platform pages.
phrases.good_example: "C'est un problème d'usurpation, pas de style — le remède est de t'assurer qu'un pseudo stylé reste clairement et uniquement le tien."

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'fiches d'écriture … à imprimer' as the standard fr printables title shape. Pair with 'gratuit' — French free-resource queries carry it as often as German ones carry 'kostenlos'.
phrases.good_example: Fiches d'écriture cursive à imprimer gratuitement — GS, CP, CE1.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'feuille de travail' or 'feuille d'exercices' — both are grammatical and both read as translated. Do not use 'fiche' for a multi-page pack; that is 'un cahier' (see the good_example pattern on French sites: 'cahier d'écriture').

phrases.english_concept: lettering (the craft of tattooed text and its style families)
phrases.register: professional but consumer-legible; used freely in French beauty/tattoo editorial
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the craft/style family ('les styles de lettrage'), keep 'police tatouage' as the search-side term (already noted on FR-019) and 'style d'écriture tatouage' as the page framing. Three distinct jobs, three distinct words.
phrases.good_example: Ton tatoueur adaptera ensuite le lettrage à ta peau : épaisseur des traits, liaisons entre les lettres.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'lettrage' where the user is choosing a font from a list — that is 'une police'. Do not import the English 'lettering' into French tattoo copy; unlike es/it, French has its own word and using the anglicism reads as a machine translation from the Spanish or Italian page.

phrases.english_concept: ASCII art, and its explicit separation from émoticône
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'art ASCII' as the French head term. When a French page needs to explain what it is NOT, borrow the three-way framing — émoticône vs art ASCII vs casseaux/dingbats — which also gives clean, natively-worded internal-link anchors between the kaomoji, ASCII-art and symbol surfaces.
phrases.good_example: L'art ASCII ne doit pas être confondu avec les émoticônes : ici on dessine avec les caractères, on ne compose pas un visage.
phrases.avoid_when: Not for single face emoticons (that's FR-020 kaomoji / émoticône). 'Casseaux' is typographers' vocabulary — use it only in a reference/explainer context, never in a title.

phrases.country_or_market: FR (also BE/CH; QC uses it too but I did not verify QC)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in any French copy touching wedding stationery. It supports the existing FR-002 (police d'écriture) target rather than competing with it.
phrases.good_example: Pour un faire-part, on garde une police élégante pour les prénoms des mariés et une police neutre pour la date.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Careful: 'faire-part' also covers birth and DEATH announcements, so an unqualified 'faire-part' in a cheerful context can misfire — always qualify it as 'faire-part de mariage' unless the context is unmistakable.

phrases.english_concept: the distinction French users themselves draw between a handwriting-style font and calligraphy
phrases.register: colloquial-but-formal-context; how real brides talk on wedding forums
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, body copy, style-description text
phrases.usage_guidance: The best available French framing for an FAQ that helps a reader pick between a casual script and a formal one. Use 'une manuscrite' / 'les manuscrites' as the noun form only in a style-picking context; elsewhere keep FR-002 (police d'écriture) as the head term.
phrases.good_example: Êtes-vous plutôt manuscrite ou calligraphie ? Les manuscrites font plus doux, la calligraphie fait plus solennel.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages — 'calligraphie' next to 'pseudo tryhard' (FR-006) or 'pseudo sweaty' (FR-028) is exactly the register collision this record exists to prevent. Also do not claim the site produces calligraphie: it produces Unicode glyphs.

phrases.native_phrase: aller à la ligne / faire un saut de ligne
phrases.english_concept: the line-break action that produces stacked text in a bio/caption
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq heading, tool copy, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use the verb form in the heading («Comment aller à la ligne dans sa bio Instagram»), because that is the query, and the noun «saut de ligne» in the tool UI and in the explanation. Reserve «retour à la ligne» for the sentence describing what the platform did — that is the register the French sources themselves use for the failure (see P8).
phrases.good_example: Pour aller à la ligne dans ta bio, ajoute un vrai saut de ligne puis copie-colle le texte.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use «texte vertical» or «à la verticale» for this — it does not match the French demand and reads as a translated CJK concept. Not a title/H1 term for the site's main generator pages; it belongs to a line-break/bio-formatting surface.

phrases.native_phrase: les sauts de ligne sont supprimés ou ignorés
phrases.english_concept: the platform silently deleting the line breaks the user inserted
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the FR FAQ heading («Pourquoi mes sauts de ligne sont-ils supprimés ?») and answer with the mechanism — an empty line containing nothing is discarded — then the fix (an invisible character, FR-011/FR-010). Naming the mechanism is what makes the invisible-character trick make sense rather than look like superstition.
phrases.good_example: Pourquoi mes sauts de ligne sont-ils supprimés ? Une ligne vide sans caractère détectable est considérée comme inutile et donc effacée.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a title/H1 term. Do not use it on pages about styled Unicode characters generally — this is a formatting failure, not a glyph failure, and mixing the two makes both answers vaguer.

phrases.english_concept: the failure-mode descriptor for a missing-glyph/tofu rendering failure
phrases.content_surface: FAQ/troubleshooting copy explaining why certain Unicode styles fail to render on some devices
phrases.avoid_when: marketing/hero copy -- this phrase is diagnostic, not promotional

phrases.english_concept: general/formal register word for 'nickname', distinct from the internet/gaming register word 'pseudo'
phrases.content_surface: useful if targeting non-gaming, general-audience nickname content; 'pseudo' remains correct for gaming/Discord contexts
phrases.avoid_when: gaming-specific pages, where 'pseudo' is the expected native term

phrases.native_phrase: signes espaces compris / espaces non compris
phrases.usage_guidance: 'compteur de signes' (2.9k/mo, CPC €3.57) is this audience; use 'signes (espaces compris)' labelling in FR counter copy for the professional register.

phrases.english_concept: alt-code method for typing special characters into a game name
phrases.usage_guidance: Use when explaining HOW to type special characters into a name field manually — a real alternative/complement to a copy-paste generator, e.g. an FAQ answer for 'comment mettre des caractères spéciaux dans mon pseudo'.
phrases.good_example: Vous pouvez aussi utiliser les codes alt (Alt+0248 pour ø) directement au clavier.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use as a page's primary term — 'caractères spéciaux' (FR-009) is the head term; this is a specific technique name, not a synonym for the concept.
